title: Judge A: PayPal engineer
brief:
You are judging a PayPal AI Hackathon (Devpost) submission as Judge A: a senior PayPal developer-relations engineer who knows PayPal's REST APIs (Orders v2, Payments, Payouts, Vault, Invoicing, Disputes, webhooks, JS SDK v6, Agent Toolkit) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) well. Be a tough, fair judge.

The submission is "Join". Read, in D:\paypal\join (read-only; do not modify anything): docs/SUBMISSION.md (the Devpost text and gallery captions), docs/screenshots/*.png (look at the images), README.md, docs/JUDGING.md, docs/TECHNICAL.md, docs/agent-run.md, docs/NEGOTIATION.md, docs/demo-video-script.md (the video is not recorded yet; judge Presentation from the text, gallery and script, and say what the video must achieve). Then check the code behind the claims that matter most to you, mainly api/src/pay/ (settle.js, paypal.js, toolkit.js), api/src/proof/mandates.js, api/src/ops.js, api/src/mcp.js. Verify claims against code; call out anything overclaimed.

Score five equally weighted criteria, 1-10 each: Technological Implementation, Design, Potential Impact, Innovation (quality of the idea), Presentation. For each: score, two or three reasons citing files or docs, and the single change that would raise it most. Then: total /50, the three most important problems (file:line where possible), and anything that is false or misleading in the docs. Keep the report under 900 words. Only report what you verified.

# Join against the judging criteria

The PayPal AI Hackathon judges five criteria with equal weight: Technological Implementation, Design, Potential
Impact, Innovation and Presentation. This page maps each one to what Join does, where it is in the code, and how to
see it in a few minutes. Every claim points to a file; the last section lists what has not been run, so nothing here
needs to be taken on trust.

**See it fast:** `npm run setup`, `npm start`, then open http://localhost:8790/demo?as=you&go=activity?agent=1 (no
keys needed; PayPal is simulated and says so). In another terminal, `npm run demo` runs four agents over MCP.
`npm test` runs 47 tests; `npm --prefix api run bench` runs the negotiation benchmark. Details: [TECHNICAL.md](TECHNICAL.md).

---

## 1. Technological Implementation

**Nine PayPal products in one money flow, each doing a job only it can do.**

| PayPal | What it does in Join | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Orders v2, intent `AUTHORIZE`, one order per payer | The organizer guarantees the whole price; each friend authorizes their own share | `api/src/pay/settle.js` `startPayment` |
| Authorizations: partial `final_capture`, void | At the lock, each share is captured, and the organizer's authorization only for what's left (whoever didn't pay); a decline or a release voids | `settle.js` `lock`, `release` |
| Captures: refund | Cancelling more than 24 hours ahead refunds everyone | `settle.js` `refundAll` |
| Payouts | The venue is paid after the game, net of fees; an organizer is paid back; a venue's extras are paid out | `settle.js` `tick` |
| Vault v3 | Save PayPal once; the person's agent pays within limits only they can set, without a redirect | `settle.js` `vaultStart`, `startPayment` |
| Invoicing v2 | A friend who joined but never paid gets an invoice; a venue bills extras | `settle.js` `requestReimbursement`, `billExtras` |
| Disputes `provide-evidence` | The moment PayPal reports a dispute, Join answers it with the booking's signed receipt and how that payer approved | `settle.js` `defend`, `webhook` |
| Webhooks: management API and `verify-webhook-signature` | Join subscribes itself to 14 events once it has a public HTTPS address, and checks every event's signature on the raw body | `api/src/server.js`, `api/src/pay/paypal.js` |
| JS SDK v6 (browser-safe client token) | The PayPal button (and Pay Later / Venmo where eligible) in a popup on Join's page | `web/src/components/PayPalButtons.jsx` |

| `PayPal-Request-Id` on every POST, journaled first | A step repeated after a crash is the same PayPal call, not a second charge | `settle.js` `paypalStep` |

For reviewers. Every claim below points to a file in the repository (`https://github.com/gino6178/join`). The section

Join's stand-in. Please challenge anything that doesn't match the code.

## 1. What Join is

Join is a marketplace for getting a group together (a sports court, a karaoke room, an escape room, a board game table,
a barbecue pit, a dinner table). People's own AI agents use it to find who is free, negotiate the price with a venue,
split the cost and settle it with PayPal.

**Join's server runs no AI model and holds no AI key.** It is the market and its rules:
- the venues' negotiation policies
- each person's spending mandate
- settlement with PayPal
- an activity log of everything the agents did

Agents reach it over MCP, REST or A2A, with a per-person token. For people without an agent, the website has its own
(§10.1): Join's server understands the request (rules, plus Qwen2.5 0.5B through its own Ollama) and the page calls the
same operations with the person's session.

## 6. Settlement (api/src/pay/settle.js)

### 6.1 States

| From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|
| (deal agreed) | a unit is held for the organizer | `awaiting_organizer` |
| `awaiting_organizer` | the organizer authorizes the **whole** total | `held` |
| `awaiting_organizer` | 10 minutes pass (`ORGANIZER_MS`) | `released` (nothing charged) |
| `held` | every invitee who joined has authorized, or 20 minutes pass (`SHARES_MS`) | `locking` → `locked` |
| `awaiting_organizer`, `held` | the organizer cancels | `cancelled` (every authorization voided) |
| `locked` | the organizer cancels at least 24 hours before the start | `refunded` (every capture refunded) |
| `locked` | the end time passes | `played` |
| `played` | Payouts to the venue (net of fees) | `venue_paid` |

### 6.2 Who pays what
- The split is even: everyone pays `floor(total / n)` and the organizer pays the remainder.
- **The organizer's order** is an Orders v2 order with intent `AUTHORIZE` for the whole total. It is the guarantee, so nobody can hold a unit for free.
- **Invitees** are invited when the booking becomes `held`, and nothing is started for them until they say yes (`pay_my_share`). Each one who joins gets their own `AUTHORIZE` order for their share.
- **On lock**, each authorized share is captured in full with `final_capture: true`. Then the organizer's authorization is captured for `total − sum(captured shares)` with `final_capture: true`, so the organizer covers anyone who didn't pay. Everything else is voided or dropped.
- **Negotiated split:** before joining, an invitee may ask for a smaller share (`proposeShare`: two asks, one open at a time). The organizer accepts or refuses (`answerShare`). Accepting moves the difference onto the organizer's share, and is refused if that would break the organizer's mandate.
- **The venue is paid after the end time,** with Payouts, of the net of captures (`seller_receivable_breakdown.net_amount`). This is because a claimed payout can't be pulled back, and cancellation stays refundable until 24 hours before the start.

### 6.3 How a payment is authorized (`startPayment`)
- **Vault:** if the person saved PayPal and `autopay` is on and the mandate fits, the order is created with `payment_source.paypal.vault_id` and authorized at once.
- **Sandbox test card:** with `PAYPAL_TEST_CARD=1`, the order is created with PayPal's published sandbox card in `payment_source.card` and authorized. This is a demo stand-in for a payer's approval, it is labelled as such in the log, and it is sandbox only.
- **Otherwise:** the order returns an approval link, `PAYER_ACTION_REQUIRED`. The person approves either through the JS SDK v6 button on the page or through the link. The return URL, polling in `tick()`, or the `CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED` webhook then call `approved()`, which authorizes the order.

finalMessage:
I scored Join **36/50**. The PayPal plumbing is real and some of the ideas are new, but the gallery and docs claim more than the code and the sandbox runs back up. I read the code read-only and changed nothing.

## Scores

**Technological Implementation: 7/10**
- The Orders v2 work is real. The organizer authorizes the whole price; at the lock each friend's share is captured and the organizer's authorization only for what's left (`settle.js:187-215`). Void, refund, Payouts, Invoicing, a Vault setup token and the Agent Toolkit calls (`toolkit.js`) all appear in the code. TECHNICAL.md §12 honestly lists which of these ran on the sandbox.
- Every payment in the gallery (02, 03, 04, 09) used PayPal's sandbox test card, sent as a raw card number from the server. Three things never ran on the sandbox: a buyer approving in the JS SDK v6 popup, an agent paying from saved PayPal (a `vault_id` order), and paying the venue after the game (TECHNICAL §12, "only against the stand-in").
- The crash-safety claim doesn't hold. The journal is written but never read back, and a booking left in `locking` after a crash is never picked up again (`settle.js:41,189`; nothing else handles that state).
- **Biggest single raise:** fix the lock retry path (problem 1 below), and run one real buyer approval and one saved-PayPal payment on the sandbox.

**Design: 8/10**
- Good agent UX. The Activity page is written by code, not a model (09). The agent states the deal's terms before it haggles (02). The demo panel plays all four friends from one window (03). On Bryntum Scheduler, payment state drives the booking bar (06).
- Some labels mislead. Hana's demo-panel click shows on Activity as "Tomás's agent" (09). The receipt page in 08 says "no witness has cosigned it yet", while its caption says "witnessed".
- **Biggest single raise:** label demo-panel steps as demo on the Activity page, and show one real PayPal approval screen in the gallery.

**Potential Impact: 6/10**
- The problem is real: someone fronts the money, nobody holds a room for free, and no-shows get billed.
- The money flow doesn't hold up in production. Join captures everything to its own account, then pays venues and organizers back with Payouts (`settle.js:273-282, 417-426`). That makes Join a merchant of record holding other people's money. They admit multiparty isn't built (README, "Why Payouts and not multiparty (yet)").
- The town is made up and no venue was involved (TECHNICAL §13 item 11).
- **Biggest single raise:** a working multiparty path (venue as `payee`, `platform_fees`), even if only partly built, plus one real venue's interest.

**Innovation: 8/10**
- The organizer's authorization as the thing that makes an agent deal binding is a sharp idea, and so is the concession schedule that stops binary search for the floor (NEGOTIATION.md, with LLM-buyer transcripts).
- Receipts in a transparency log with witness cosignatures is unusual and well done.
- The AP2 part is mostly circular. Join signs the mandate, hands it to the agent, then checks that the agent sends back the exact same string (`mandates.js:60-61`). That adds nothing beyond the database limit check; TECHNICAL §13 item 0 admits Join is both provider and verifier.
- **Biggest single raise:** have the person sign mandates with their own key (a passkey), or have PayPal check them.

**Presentation: 7/10**
- The docs are unusually thorough and honest about what hasn't run (JUDGING.md's last section).
- There is no video yet. SUBMISSION.md lines 44-51 still hold an old gallery table pointing at files that don't exist (`1-activity.png`, `0-sign-in.png`). The "See it fast" link in JUDGING.md:8 is malformed (`go=activity?agent=1`).
- **What the video must achieve:** show one real PayPal approval rather than only the test card, a capture happening at the lock, and the over-limit refusal. Keep it under 3 minutes.

**Total: 36/50**
